function: Excluded (function): the network classifies which of 13 NR DM-RS patterns to use in the next slot (p. 2, Eq. 6); no channel estimate or prediction is output.
notes: Step 1 in order: a 5-page research letter (not an editorial), not a survey, a learned component exists (ViViT/CNN classifier, p. 3), and it acts on the physical layer (DM-RS), so the function check decides. p. 2: 'the proposed CPRS framework directly classifies the optimal allocation' from the uplink CSI, among '|P| = 13 possible allocations'; the labels come from an exhaustive search of throughput (p. 4). The proposed model outputs no channel estimate, compressed CSI or predicted channel; the channel predictor with NMSE -8.42 dB (p. 4) belongs only to the 'Disjoint' baseline. Reported metrics are allocation accuracy (Table II, p. 4) and throughput (Fig. 4, p. 5). Choosing the DM-RS pattern is a reference-signal configuration decision of the link-adaptation type, which is outside the seven areas. BORDERLINE: the paper frames CPRS as channel-prediction-based and as a way to reduce CSI feedback (p. 1), so the reviewer may reassign it to area 2. Facts for a reassignment: Sionna ray tracing of the street-canyon-with-cars scene, 8x8 BS array, 2x1 UE, band n1, random 8:1:1 split with no unseen condition (p. 4); baselines DRL [24], Disjoint ViViT/CNN, Maximize Data Symbols, Random Average (p. 4); ViViT complexity O(L(N^2 D + N D^2)) and about 1.082e9 FLOPs (pp. 3-4); no code or data link. The PDF is the arXiv 2507.11064v2 preprint (p. 1) and carries no DOI.
